topic: Burley Disney roughness-driven diffuse retroreflection vs flat Lambertian missing rim sheen rig
topic_zh: Burley 迪士尼粗糙度驱动漫反射逆反射对比平坦 Lambert 漫反射边缘丝绒感缺失
scope: Deterministic Brent Burley (SIGGRAPH 2012 Disney Principled BRDF) roughness-driven diffuse retroreflection (M_Burley = (1 + (F_D90 - 1)*(1 - mu)^5)^2, F_D90 = 0.5 + 2*r*cos^2(theta_d)) via a 5-op Schlick power chain versus naive flat Lambertian diffuse (M = 1.0) and 64-strip angular quadrature across 17 viewing cosine stations (NdotV in [0.05, 0.85]). No neural material capture execution.

robustness.name: Sampled 17 viewing cosine stations preserve MERL-calibrated grazing retroreflection on rough surfaces

good_fit: Rough matte materials (terracotta, dry earth, moon dust, chalk, unglazed ceramics, felt) in Disney Principled BRDF, Frostbite, and Unity HDRP
Explaining why constant Lambertian diffuse loses -78.58% (-3.6685x) of the grazing retroreflective rim on rough surfaces
Coupling diffuse grazing reflectance F_D90 = 0.5 + 2·r·cos²θ_d directly to the specular roughness parameter r
Evaluating (1 - μ)^5 via a 3-multiply register chain instead of transcendental pow(1 - μ, 5.0)
not_for: Pure metallic conductors (metallic = 1.0) where diffuse reflectance ρ is zero
Mirror-smooth dielectrics where specular Fresnel dominates the grazing rim
Neural SVBRDF capture or photo-to-material diffusion models
Subsurface-dominated translucent wax or jade where deep volumetric scattering dominates surface V-cavities
